content_voiceover: This slide stacks three trials together to show the evolution of frontline regimens for advanced Hodgkin lymphoma, and it's worth tracing the sequence. On the left is BrECADD, a PET-adapted regimen combining brentuximab vedotin with etoposide, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, dacarbazine, and dexamethasone, tested here specifically in older patients, ages 61 to 75, a population that tolerates standard intensified regimens poorly. With interim PET-guided cycle number, two-year progression-free survival was 91.5 percent and 82 percent achieved complete response, published in the Lancet in 2024, showing this de-escalated, biomarker-guided approach works even in an older, more fragile population. On the right are two head-to-head comparisons that map the modern treatment ladder. First, brentuximab vedotin plus AVD beat standard ABVD, that's the ECHELON-1 result we just covered, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2022. Then, nivolumab plus AVD was compared against brentuximab vedotin plus AVD in a large study of nearly a thousand patients with stage III or IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma, and at the second interim analysis, nivolumab-AVD significantly improved progression-free survival, hazard ratio 0.48, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2024. Notably, nivolumab was also better tolerated, with only 9.4 percent discontinuing treatment versus 22.2 percent on brentuximab vedotin. So the ladder is ABVD, then brentuximab vedotin-AVD beats ABVD, then nivolumab-AVD beats brentuximab vedotin-AVD, reflecting the field's steady move toward checkpoint inhibitor-based frontline therapy.
keypoints: SWOG S1826: Nivo-AVD > BV+AVD, HR 0.48, stage III/IV cHL - NEJM 2024;391:1379
Nivo-AVD better tolerated: 9.4% discontinuation vs 22.2% with BV-AVD
Treatment evolution ladder: ABVD -> BV+AVD -> Nivo-AVD
keypoint_voiceover: Trace the frontline treatment ladder for advanced classical Hodgkin lymphoma: brentuximab vedotin plus AVD beat ABVD in ECHELON-1, then nivolumab plus AVD beat brentuximab vedotin plus AVD in the SWOG S1826 trial, with a hazard ratio of 0.48 and fewer discontinuations. And for older, less fit patients, BrECADD with PET-adapted dosing achieved a 91.5 percent two-year progression-free survival.
